title: Text Editors, Browser Developer Tools, Saving and Refreshing
learningObjectives: Explain why a text editor is used to write code
Save a file with an appropriate name and open it in a browser
Identify beginner uses of the Elements panel and Console in developer tools
Explain the relationship between saving a change and refreshing a page

understand.concept: A text editor is a tool for writing and changing code as plain text. A browser displays the web page. Browser developer tools help inspect page structure, applied styles and JavaScript errors. After changing code, save the file; refresh the browser page to load the saved change.
understand.whyItMatters: A reliable edit-save-refresh routine prevents confusion between old and new code. Developer tools let you inspect evidence instead of guessing when something goes wrong.
understand.history: Early web workflows used separate tools for editing and viewing pages. Browsers gradually gained built-in developer tools for inspecting page structure, styles, network activity and errors.
understand.analogy: A text editor is like writing instructions in a notebook. Saving preserves the instructions; the browser shows the result produced from them. Developer tools are an inspection window.
understand.analogyLimit: A browser does more than read notes: it parses HTML, calculates CSS and executes JavaScript. Temporary edits made in developer tools do not automatically change the original file.

explain.narrative: Open an HTML file in a text editor and change its heading. Save the file. Open that file in a browser and refresh it; the new heading should appear. Open developer tools and inspect the HTML structure in the Elements panel. The Console displays JavaScript messages and errors. When an error appears, note its first line, filename and line number. A live edit in developer tools is temporary; make permanent changes in the source file and save it.

examples.code:
1. Open index.html in a text editor
2. Change the heading text
3. Save the file
4. Refresh the page in the browser
5. Observe the updated heading
examples.explanation: If you do not save, the browser may not receive the new change. If you do not refresh, you may still see the previously loaded page. Caching can sometimes require a hard refresh, but begin with a normal refresh.
examples.expectedOutput: The browser displays the updated heading.

practise.guidedTask: Change a paragraph in index.html, save and refresh. Then locate that paragraph in the Elements panel of developer tools.
practise.independentTask: Introduce one small intentional mistake in a practice page. Observe the browser and check the Console for an error. Correct the source file, save and refresh.
hints: First confirm that the source file was saved.
Elements shows document structure; Console shows messages and errors.
Edits made in developer tools are not automatically saved to the source file.

questions.prompt: What is the usual order after editing a source file?
questions.explanation: Save the source change first, then refresh the browser page to load it.

questions.prompt: Where can you usually inspect JavaScript errors?
questions.explanation: The Console displays JavaScript errors, warnings and messages.
